parameters.content:
## Job Scout: daily scan

Every morning this path scans the Ashby, Greenhouse and Lever boards listed in **Job Scout config**, saves one lead per posting in the `leads` Data Table, marks leads whose postings are gone as closed, scores the leads that pass the hard filters, and sends the best ones to Telegram.

**Setup**
1. Create a bot with @BotFather and pick its credential on **Send header**, **Send lead message** and **Send crash alert**.
2. Add a Bearer Auth credential with your TypeSafe API key on **Ask Jev** and **Ask Jev again**, and an Anthropic credential on **Write fit line**.
3. Fill in **Job Scout config** (see the note below it), including your **profileSummary**.
4. Publish the workflow. The **Applied**, **Referral** and **Pass** buttons on each lead call this workflow's webhooks and form, so they work only while it's published (see Action links and Pass form).

The `leads`, `state`, `referrals` and `passes` tables are created on the first run if they don't exist. Job Scout never applies for jobs or contacts anyone.

## Job Scout config

Edit these fields in the **Job Scout config** node:

- **ashbyBoards**: Ashby board names to scan, as a list. The board name is the part after `jobs.ashbyhq.com/` in a company's job board link. Default: `n8n`, `posthog`, `ramp`.
- **greenhouseBoards**: Greenhouse board names, the part after `boards.greenhouse.io/` or `job-boards.greenhouse.io/` in a company's Greenhouse job board link. Default: `instacart`.
- **leverBoards**: Lever site names, the part after `jobs.lever.co/` in a company's Lever job board link. Default: `palantir`, `spotify`.
- A board whose list can't be fetched is skipped for that scan, and none of its leads are marked closed.
- **telegramChatId**: the chat the daily ping goes to. Tap Start in your bot, open `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getUpdates` once, and copy `message.chat.id`.
- **dailyCap**: the most leads one daily ping sends. Leads over the cap stay New and go out on a later day. Default 10.
- **tablePrefix**: put in front of every Data Table name, so `jobscout_` gives `jobscout_leads`. n8n looks tables up by a "name contains" match, so no other table name may contain the full name (for example, don't use an empty prefix if `jobscout_leads` exists). The tests use `jobscout_test_`.
- **roleFamilies**: the kinds of roles you want, each with a `name`, a `description` and the `titleKeywords` that mark it. Jev picks a lead's family from these (or none of them), and every family scores the same. They don't filter anything. Default: DevEx/Product PM, FDE/Solutions, Product/Frontend Engineering, and DevRel/DevEx.
- **excludedTitles**: a posting whose title contains one of these words or phrases is filtered out. Case doesn't matter and only whole words match, so `Finance` doesn't match "Fintech" and `HR` doesn't match "HRIS". Only the title is checked, never the department: developer relations roles often sit in Marketing. Default: non-engineering operations titles (Accountant, Finance, Legal, Counsel, Paralegal, HR, People Ops, Office Manager, Facilities, Executive Assistant). `Marketing` is deliberately not on the list.
- **excludedTitleOverrides**: a title that contains one of these words is never excluded, so "Software Engineer, Finance Platform" is kept while "Finance Manager" is filtered out. Same whole-word matching. Default: Engineer, Engineering, Developer, Software, SWE, Architect, Programmer, Advocate, DevRel, Product Manager, PM, Platform.
- **locationRules**:
  - `usRemote`: keep postings that offer remote work in the US, including ones where "Remote (US)" is only a secondary location. Default `true`.
  - `usCountryNames`: the names that count as the US.
  - `metros`: areas where you'd also take non-remote work. Each has `cities`, `regions` (if a posting states a state, it must be one of these) and `workplaceTypes` (`Remote`, `Hybrid`, `OnSite`; Lever's and Greenhouse's workplace types are mapped to these). Default: Dallas–Fort Worth with its suburbs, remote, hybrid or on-site. Austin is not in the list, so only remote US roles based there pass.
  - A posting with no location, or one that can't be placed, passes and shows as "Location unclear".
- **payFloor**: the lowest yearly base pay you'd take, in US dollars. A posting is filtered out only when its stated USD base salary range tops out below the floor. Equity, bonus and commission don't count. Hourly pay counts at 2,080 hours a year. No stated pay, or pay in another currency, passes; the message shows the posting's pay text or "Pay not listed". Default 180000.

- **profileSummary**: a few short lines about you: target roles, core stack, years of experience, domains, the seniority you want, and location. Jev judges stack and domain fit against it, and Claude writes each lead's fit line from it. Keep it short and factual, and don't paste a resume. Changing it makes Jev judge the unsent leads again on the next scan.
- **weights**: points for each sub-score: `roleFamily`, `stack`, `seniority`, `location`, `domain`, `freshness` and `referral`. They're scaled to add up to 100. Default 25, 20, 15, 15, 10, 10, 5. The referral points go to every lead from a company you've tapped **Referral** on. A weight change re-ranks leads on the next scan without new Jev calls.
- **targetSeniority**: the levels that get full seniority points, from Jev's levels `intern_junior`, `mid`, `senior`, `lead`, `staff_plus`, `manager` and `founding`. A posting that states no level gets half the points, and any other level a fifth. Default `senior`, `lead`, `founding`.
- **minFitScore**: the lowest fit score a lead can be sent with. Default 60.
- **freshnessWindowDays**: how many days after Job Scout first sees a lead it can still be sent; only leads inside the window are judged by Jev. Separately, the freshness sub-score falls from full to zero as the posting ages (counted from the earlier of its publish date and first sighting) across the same number of days, so an old posting found today can still be sent but ranks lower. Default 30.
- **jevModel**: the TypeSafe Jev model version. It's pinned so scores don't shift when TypeSafe ships a new version; changing it makes Jev judge the unsent leads again. Default `jev-1.13.0`.

**Run time** is set on the **Daily scan** trigger, not here, because a trigger's settings can't read other nodes. Default 8:00 in the instance timezone. If n8n is down at that time, the most recent missed scan runs when it comes back.

## Save leads

A lead is keyed by `<ats>:<board>:<job id>`, such as `greenhouse:instacart:7144697`. Every ATS is saved with the same fields.

- **Save lead** upserts on that key, so a second scan updates the posting fields and `last_seen_at` instead of adding a row. It also clears `closed_at`, so a posting that is listed again is open again.
- **Mark first sighting** gives rows with no status yet `status = new` and `first_seen_at = now`. Rows that already have a status keep their first-seen date.

## Daily ping

- **Pick leads to send** chooses leads with status `new`, not closed, `filter_result` `passed`, a role family, a fit score of at least **minFitScore**, first seen within the freshness window and with no `sent_at`, highest fit score first, up to `dailyCap`. Leads over the cap stay New and compete again on later scans.
- **Send header** sends "Job Scout: N new leads today" with sound. When Jev couldn't score some leads, it adds "· N couldn't be scored (retrying next scan)".
- On a day with nothing to send, it sends one silent message instead: "Job Scout: no new leads today", with how many postings were scanned, how many were filtered out, and how many couldn't be scored.
- Each lead goes out as its own silent message, one per second, with **Open posting** and **Search LinkedIn** buttons and, below them, signed **Applied**, **Referral** and **Pass** buttons (see Action links and Pass form). "Referral available" follows the company name when the company has a referral. It shows the pay text (or a salary found in the description, or "Pay not listed"), the location or "Location unclear", the fit score with its points per sub-score, and Claude's fit line (left out if Claude failed for that lead).
- **Search LinkedIn** opens LinkedIn's own people search (`linkedin.com/search/results/people/?keywords=`, an unofficial URL format) for the company plus a short form of the title. Job Scout makes no LinkedIn calls. The short form drops anything in brackets, cuts the title at the first comma, `|`, spaced hyphen or en or em dash, and drops leading seniority words (Senior, Sr, Staff, Principal, Lead, Junior, Jr, Founding, Associate) and a trailing level (I to V, L1 to L99, a single digit). If that leaves one word, the next part is added. "Senior Software Engineer II, AI Labs & Foundations" at Instacart searches "Instacart Software Engineer"; "Director, Customer Experience" at ramp searches "ramp Director Customer Experience".
- **Mark sent** sets `sent_at` and saves the fit line right after each message, so no lead is sent twice.

Both Telegram nodes use HTML parse mode and have the n8n attribution line turned off.

## Hard filters

**Apply hard filters** checks every posting on every scan against the rules in **Job Scout config**, in this order: location, pay floor, excluded titles.

- The first rule a posting breaks is saved in its lead's `filter_result`: `location`, `pay_floor` or `excluded_title`. A posting that breaks none gets `passed`.
- Filtered leads stay in the `leads` table and are never sent.
- Every scan checks again, so a rule you edit also applies to leads saved earlier.
- Unknown pay or location never fails a rule.
- An excluded title word doesn't count when the title also has a word from `excludedTitleOverrides`, such as Engineer or Developer.

Location reads each posting's workplace type and locations: Ashby's location, secondary locations and addresses (not `isRemote`, which Ashby sets on many hybrid postings); Greenhouse's location name, which also gives the workplace type; and Lever's location, all locations and country code. `location_basis` says why a lead passed: `us_remote`, `metro` or `unclear`. `pay_min` and `pay_max` hold the stated USD base salary per year, when there is one.

options.system: You write one sentence for a job seeker's Telegram message saying why a job posting fits them. Use only facts written in the posting or in the job seeker's profile summary. Do not invent or assume anything that isn't written there: no years of experience, skills, employers, achievements, team details, pay or locations that aren't stated. Name one or two overlaps, and count something as an overlap only when the posting itself names it and the profile names the same thing; don't match look-alike words. If the fit is weak, say plainly what does match. Write one sentence of at most 30 words, in plain text, with no quotes, emoji or preamble.

parameters.content:
## Scoring

Only leads that passed the filters, are New and unsent, and were first seen within **freshnessWindowDays** are scored.

- **Build Jev requests** builds one request per lead for TypeSafe's Jev, with every question in it: role family (from the title and duties, never the department), stack fit and domain fit against **profileSummary**, whether the posting names a stack, and the seniority level. For a posting with no structured pay, a regex finds dollar amounts in the description and Jev picks the base salary among them, or none.
- A lead is judged again only when its request changes: a new profile summary, role families, model, or posting text. Weights, **targetSeniority** and **minFitScore** are applied in code, so editing them costs no Jev calls.
- **Ask Jev** uses a Bearer Auth credential with your TypeSafe API key (console.typesafe.ai/keys). It sends each request once. The requests that fail go to **Ask Jev again** for a second try, and if the first of those fails too, all of them are tried up to twice more, 5 seconds apart. A lead whose request still fails is saved as unscored, isn't sent, is counted in the header, and is judged again on the next scan.
- **Score and select** combines the sub-scores with **weights** into a fit score out of 100, every scan. Location, freshness and referral are computed in code. A salary Jev found in the description that tops out below **payFloor** sets `filter_result` to `pay_floor`.
- A lead whose role family is "None of these" (Jev's top answer) is never sent, whatever its fit score.
- Each lead's `selection_reason` says what holds it back: `closed`, `unscored`, `pay_floor`, `no_role_family`, `window_passed` (first seen too long ago), `below_min_fit`, or `eligible`.
- **Pick leads to send** takes the eligible leads, highest fit first, up to **dailyCap**.
- **Write fit line** asks Claude (Anthropic credential) for one sentence on why each picked lead fits, using only the posting and the profile summary. Claude runs only for leads that are sent. If Claude fails for a lead, the lead goes out without a fit line.

Jev costs about $0.0002 per judged lead. Each lead's sub-scores, fit score, Jev's raw answers and the fit line are saved in the `leads` table.

## Closed postings

- **Get open leads** reads every lead with no `closed_at`.
- **Find closed leads** picks the ones from boards fetched successfully in this scan whose postings are no longer listed, whatever their status.
- **Mark closed** sets their `closed_at`. Nothing is sent about it. A closed lead is never judged or sent, and its `selection_reason` becomes `closed`.
- A board whose fetch failed closes nothing. If a closed posting is listed again, **Save lead** clears `closed_at`.

## Crash alert

If a scan fails, **Scan crashed** runs and **Send crash alert** sends "Job Scout scan failed at <step>: <error>" to the chat in **Job Scout config**, with a link to the failed execution.

- **Nothing to hook up after import.** Importing a template drops workflow settings, so this doesn't use one: when a workflow has an Error Trigger and no error workflow is chosen in its settings, n8n runs that workflow's own Error Trigger when one of its runs fails. Leave **Settings → Error workflow** empty (or pick this workflow). Picking another workflow there sends the alert to that one instead.
- It fires for published runs only (the daily schedule), not when you click Execute in the editor, and it runs the published version.
- Pick your Telegram credential on **Send crash alert**.
- The chat ID is read from **telegramChatId** in **Job Scout config** without running that node, so keep that field a plain value, not an expression.
- If no board could be fetched at all, the scan fails at **Normalize postings** on purpose, so you get this alert instead of an empty day.

parameters.content:
## Every run: tables, secret, route

Every trigger runs **Job Scout config** and this setup, then **Route by trigger** sends the run down its own path: the daily scan, **Applied**, **Referral** or **Pass**.

- The `leads`, `state`, `referrals` and `passes` tables are created if they don't exist.
- **Get referrals** reads the companies with a referral, for scoring.
- **Signing secret**: the key that signs action links. On the first run **Generate signing secret** makes 32 random bytes (hex) and saves them in the `state` table as `signing_secret`. It isn't in the config, the messages or the template.

## Action links: Applied and Referral

Each lead message has **Applied** and **Referral** buttons. They open this workflow's GET webhooks `/webhook/job-scout/applied` and `/webhook/job-scout/referral` with `lead` (the lead key) and `sig` in the query string, and show a short page.

- **Signature:** HMAC-SHA256 of `<action>:<lead key>` with the signing secret, first 32 hex characters. A wrong or missing signature gets "Invalid link" (403) and changes nothing. Links don't expire. To revoke every link, delete the `signing_secret` row in `state`; the next run makes a new one.
- **Applied:** a New or Picked lead becomes `applied` with `applied_at`, and is never sent again. A second tap changes nothing; a Passed lead isn't changed (409). **Pass** has its own form (see Pass form).
- **Referral:** saves the lead's company in `referrals` (key: the name in lower case, letters and digits only). Every current and future lead from that company gets the referral points and shows "Referral available". Its unsent leads are rescored at once, with no Jev calls.
- **URLs** come from n8n itself: `$execution.resumeUrl` is built from the instance's public webhook URL (`WEBHOOK_URL` or `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL`), and the links use n8n's default `webhook/` prefix. Set that URL to an address your phone can reach.
- **Publish** the workflow: production webhooks answer only while it's published. **Ignore Bots** is on, so link previewers get a 403 and nothing happens.
- Anyone who can read the `state` table or this workflow's saved executions can make valid links.

parameters.content:
## Pass form

Each lead message has a **Pass** button. It opens this workflow's form at `/form/job-scout/pass` with `lead`, `sig` (signed `pass:<lead key>`), and the lead's `title` and `company` in the query string. `lead` and `sig` fill the form's hidden fields; the title and company are only shown on the form.

- **Reason** is required, one of the ten pass reasons (label: saved code):
  - Comp below range: `comp_below_range`
  - Wrong seniority: `seniority_mismatch`
  - Not my role family: `role_family_off`
  - Remote claim is soft: `location_not_real`
  - Company stage off: `company_stage_off`
  - Stack mismatch: `tech_stack_off`
  - Already applied: `already_applied`
  - Not interested: `no_interest`
  - Listing looks wrong: `listing_looks_wrong`
  - Stale repost: `stale_repost`
- **Anything else?** is an optional note.
- **On submit:** a wrong or missing signature gets "Invalid link" and changes nothing; a missing reason gets "Pick a reason". A New or Picked lead becomes `passed` with `passed_at`, its reason and note are saved in `passes` (one row per lead), and it is never sent again. Passing it again replaces the reason and note and keeps the first date. An Applied lead isn't changed.
- **Form Trigger version 2.1:** later versions refuse to run when a Respond to Webhook node follows them, and every trigger here leads to **Show page**. Version 2.1 answers the form through **Show page**, so the page after Pass shows what happened.
- **Publish** the workflow: the form's production URL works only while it's published. **Ignore Bots** is on.

nodeGroups.name: Setup
nodeGroups.description: Runs for every trigger: creates missing tables, reads the referrals, and reads the signing secret for action links (made on the first run).

nodeGroups.name: Fetch boards
nodeGroups.description: Fetches each Ashby, Greenhouse and Lever board in the config, and turns each posting into a lead with the same fields.

nodeGroups.name: Save leads
nodeGroups.description: Upserts each lead on its key (clearing closed_at for postings listed again), then marks leads seen for the first time as New.

nodeGroups.name: Score leads
nodeGroups.description: Jev judges New, unsent leads that passed the filters when their input changed (failed requests get a second try); code totals the fit score.

nodeGroups.name: Build the ping
nodeGroups.description: Picks the top eligible leads up to the daily cap, has Claude write fit lines, and sends the header, or a 'no new leads' message with counts.

nodeGroups.name: Send each lead
nodeGroups.description: Sends one silent message per lead with Open posting, Applied, Referral and Pass buttons and saves sent_at and the fit line, one per second.

nodeGroups.name: Crash alert
nodeGroups.description: Runs when a published run of this workflow fails and sends the failed step and the error to Telegram.
